public_rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. It applies only if OpenAI falls. The contract reads that as a WeWork-style collapse or a steep valuation crash. None of the cited items shows that this has happened. On 2026-02-27, OpenAI announced $110B in new investment at a $730B pre-money valuation. That included $30B from SoftBank, $30B from NVIDIA and $50B from Amazon (e2). In an update dated 2026-03-31, Engadget reported OpenAI's announcement that the round closed at $122B, with a post-money valuation of $852B (e1). Both items are from February and March 2026. They do not cover OpenAI's later condition. The condition has not been shown to be met, and there is no evidence about losses at investors or partners. So the forecast cannot be scored yet, and it remains open.
limitations: The source does not define 'falls'. This assessment reads it as a collapse or a steep valuation crash.
The cited evidence ends in March 2026. It does not show OpenAI's valuation or financial condition from April to October 2026.
The funding items show who invested. They show no losses or distress for SoftBank or anyone else.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If OpenAI falls, many parties besides SoftBank will struggle with the fallout.

statement.excerpt: If OpenAI falls, SoftBank will hardly be alone in struggling to pick the pieces.

our_interpretation: Antecedent: OpenAI 'falls', read as a collapse, near-bankruptcy or steep valuation crash like WeWork's, the comparison he draws.
Outcome: investors or partners other than SoftBank also suffer substantial losses or distress.
criteria.support_condition: OpenAI collapses or crashes in value, and parties besides SoftBank report substantial losses or distress from it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: OpenAI collapses or crashes in value, and SoftBank alone bears substantial losses.
